findings.title: SQL injection in data migration
findings.body: The migration interpolates the host string read from `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` directly into a raw `execute` SQL statement: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. Hosts come from admin-entered free text. A host value containing an apostrophe (e.g. `foo's.example.com`) or a multi-statement payload (e.g. `evil'); DROP TABLE users; --`) will break the migration or execute arbitrary SQL, since `execute` runs as a single connection.exec (multiple statements allowed). Use a parameterized query or, better, instantiate the model: `EmbeddableHost.create!(host: h, category_id: category_id)`.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')`. If the model is built/saved with `host: nil` (which happens when an admin submits the form with no host, or with a malformed JSON body, or when a malicious POST sends `embeddable_host[host]=`), `nil.sub!` raises `NoMethodError`, bypassing the format validator and surfacing as a 500 error instead of a clean validation failure (422). It should guard with `self.host &&` or use non-mutating assignment.

findings.title: update/destroy crash when record not found
findings.body: `update` and `destroy` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call methods on `host` (e.g. `save_host(host)`, `host.destroy`) without checking whether it was found. Any PUT/DELETE with a non-existent or non-numeric id (including requests where the record was concurrently removed) will raise `NoMethodError` on nil and return a 500. Should `return not_found` (or render 404) when the lookup yields nil.

findings.title: save_host does not guard against missing embeddable_host param
findings.body: `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` is always present. A request without the `embeddable_host` key (malformed body, blank form submission, or an attacker-controlled POST) raises `NoMethodError` on nil. Guard with `return render_json_error(...)` or `params.require(:embeddable_host).permit(...)` so the controller responds with a clear 400/422 instead of a 500.

findings.title: Host regex rejects valid long-TLD domains
findings.body: `\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` caps the TLD at 5 letters. Legitimate gTLDs longer than 5 chars exist (e.g. `.museum`, `.travel`, `.coop` happens to fit, but `.technology`, `.international`, `.directory` etc. all fail). The format validator should accept TLDs of at least 2 characters, e.g. `\.[a-z]{2,}` (and case-insensitively since `/i` is used).

findings.title: Imported topic ends up with nil category if record_for_host misses
findings.body: Previously the imported topic was forced into `SiteSetting.embed_category`; now it is forced into `eh.try(:category_id)`. `record_for_host` returns false when no row matches, so on a race (host deleted between `TopicRetriever.invalid_host?` and `TopicEmbed.import`) the post is created with `category: nil` and falls through `Topic#ensure_topic_has_a_category` to the uncategorized category — bypassing any admin-configured per-host category and silently breaking the embed flow. Either fail loudly (return nil and let the job retry) or fall back to a clearly documented default category rather than silently degrading to uncategorized.

findings.title: Controller spec is a stub; create/update/destroy untested
findings.body: The new `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` spec only asserts inheritance from `Admin::AdminController`. The real surface area — `create`, `update`, `destroy`, the `save_host` flow, and the nil-record handling — has zero coverage, which is why the bugs above (nil host in `save_host`, nil record in update/destroy) are invisible to CI. At minimum, add specs that exercise create with a valid host, update with an unknown id (expect 404), and destroy with an unknown id.

findings.title: EmbeddingController spec is a stub
findings.body: Same problem: the only assertion is that the class is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController`. There is no coverage for `show`, `update`, the `fetch_embedding` before-filter, or the OpenStruct payload it builds. Add at least one request spec for `GET /admin/customize/embedding` that asserts the returned JSON includes `embeddable_hosts` with the correct shape.

findings.title: Missing model tests for nil/blank/invalid hosts
findings.body: The new model spec only exercises three happy paths (`http://`, `https://`, path trimming) and `host_allowed?` lookups. There is no test for `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?`, no test for invalid hosts (e.g. `not a host`, `localhost`, long-TLD hosts like `.museum`), no test that an existing record returns its hosts from `record_for_host` case-insensitively, and no test that creating two hosts with the same name is (or isn't) permitted. These would catch the nil-host crash, the TLD regex bug, and duplicate-host data integrity issues.

findings.title: Serializer duplicates attributes via both macro and methods
findings.body: `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` is declared at the top of the class, and then each of those three attributes is also defined as an explicit method returning `object.<attr>`. With `ApplicationSerializer` (ActiveModel::Serializer), `attributes` already wires the methods, so the explicit `def id/def host/def catbody_id` definitions are dead code that obscure the contract. Either drop the explicit methods or drop the `attributes` macro; doing both is confusing and risks subtle regressions if the serializer base class changes its convention.

findings.title: Dead translation key admin.embedding.edit
findings.body: The new locale block adds `edit: "edit"` under `admin.embedding`, but no template, component, or JS file references `admin.embedding.edit` (the only edit-related string is `admin.embedding.confirm_delete`). Remove the unused key to keep the locale file aligned with the UI.
